think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 25-year-old female presents with subacute dull mid-back pain radiating anteriorly to the breast/precordium for 3 months. Plain radiography and MRI reveal scalloping of the T7 vertebral body, pedicle erosion, and an enhancing destructive paraspinal/costotransverse soft-tissue mass abutting the descending aorta. Differentiating this isolated articular lesion from an aggressive primary osseous neoplasm (such as osteoblastoma, chondrosarcoma, or giant cell tumor) or metastatic disease versus pyogenic septic arthritis is challenging, given the absence of pulmonary symptoms, fever, or classical spinal gibbus deformity.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage concludes after physical examination, inflammatory markers, viral serological testing, thoracic spine plain radiography, and thoracic spine MRI characterizing the T7 periarticular lesion, immediately before CT-guided percutaneous biopsy and molecular GeneXpert testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Primary bone malignancy or metastasis (ruled out by absence of malignant cytological features on CT-guided biopsy, which demonstrated caseous necrosis and Langhans giant cells), pyogenic bacterial costotransverse septic arthritis (ruled out by the indolent 3-month course, mild inflammatory marker elevation, and presence of caseating granulomas rather than acute neutrophilic suppuration), and non-infectious inflammatory spondyloarthropathy (ruled out by destructive cortical scalloping and positive mycobacterial testing).
case_prompt:
A 25-year-old female presented with dull left mid-back pain of 3 months' duration. The pain was moderate in intensity and radiated anteriorly toward the left breast and precordium. Physical examination revealed focal tenderness over the inferior angle of the left scapula and 7th costovertebral junction, without overlying soft-tissue swelling or erythema. Neurological examination was normal.

Laboratory investigations demonstrated an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 40 mm/hr and a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 6 mg/L. Serological testing for HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen, and hepatitis C antibody was negative.

Anteroposterior plain radiographs of the thoracic spine demonstrated left-sided scalloping of the T7 vertebral body, with cortical erosion of the left T7 pedicle and the adjacent rib head. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thoracic spine revealed a left-sided T7 enhancing periarticular erosive lesion, marked bone marrow edema in the posteromedial aspect of the left 7th rib, the left posterolateral T7 vertebral body, and the lateral left T7 pedicle. There was associated thickening and enhancement of the synovium of the left 7th costotransverse joint, with an enhancing soft-tissue mass elevating the overlying pleura and directly abutting the descending aorta.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary osseous neoplasm or thoracic metastasis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Cortical scalloping and erosion of the T7 vertebral body, pedicle, and adjacent rib head with an expansive paraspinal mass abutting the descending aorta raised strong clinical suspicion for a malignant or aggressive bone tumor, but percutaneous biopsy revealed caseating granulomas without neoplastic cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The anteroposterior X-rays of the thoracic spine showed that the T7 vertebral body was scalloped on the left side, and there erosion of the T7 left pedicle and adjoining rib [Figure 1].

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Acute pyogenic arthritis typically presents with rapid onset, high fever, marked leukocytosis, and acute suppuration, whereas this patient exhibited an indolent 3-month clinical course, mild inflammatory markers, and chronic granulomatous synovial proliferation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A 25-year-old female presented with the left dull mid-back pain for 3 months' duration.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of the left 7th costotransverse mass demonstrated caseous necrosis with epithelioid histiocytes and Langerhans giant cells, corroborated by GeneXpert detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis susceptible to isoniazid and rifampicin.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A CT-guided biopsy was diagnostic for TB; it demonstrated caseous necrosis with epithelioid and Langerhans giant cells [Figure 3]. In addition, GeneXpert detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis that showed sensitivity to both isoniazid and rifampicin.

editor_comments: Rare presentation of isolated costotransverse joint tuberculous arthritis mimicking an aggressive thoracic spine malignancy. Admission prompt stops cleanly after MRI and baseline labs, prior to biopsy and GeneXpert.
